Staff Report Printout

N. Request of Councilmembers Zwick, Zernitskaya, and Hall that, in conjunction with necessary updates arising out of SB 450, and in order to facilitate diverse housing choices in the City’s highest opportunity areas, the City Council directs the City Manager and the City Attorney to return with an ordinance to amend the City’s regulations governing ministerial approval for certain lot splits and duplexes on parcels zoned for single-unit residential by: (1) removing the owner-occupancy requirement for lot splits and duplexes and clarifying that vacant or demolished parcels, as well as lots with approved demolition permits, are eligible for lot splits and duplexes, (2) allowing one roof deck per unit, and (3) ensuring that no standard within this ordinance or the underlying zoning district shall preclude the construction of 2 units, not including ADUs, of at least 1200 square feet each. One year after implementation, city staff shall return with a report on any impacts of the ordinance, as amended, including data on net new housing units permitted, effects on displacement (if any), concentration of ownership, and other pertinent information to evaluate its success in affirmatively furthering fair housing and creating more affordable “missing middle” homes.
Staff Report Printout
a. Written Comments

  CITY OF SANTA MONICA

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

  JANUARY 28, 2025

  A regular meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor Negrete at 5:34 p.m., on
  Tuesday, January 28, 2025, at City Council Chambers, 1685 Main Street, Santa Monica, CA.

  Roll Call:  Present:  Mayor Lana Negrete
  Mayor Pro Tem Caroline Torosis
  Councilmember Jesse Zwick
  Councilmember Dan Hall
  Councilmember Ellis Raskin
  Councilmember Barry Snell
  Councilmember Natalya Zernitskaya

  Also Present:  City Manager David White
  City Attorney Douglas Sloan
  City Clerk Nikima S. Newsome

  CONVENE/PLEDGE  On order of the Mayor, the City Council convened at 5:34 p.m., with all
  members present. Councilmember Raskin led the assemblage in the Pledge
  of Allegiance.

  STATEMENT OF  The City of Santa Monica is located on the land of Tovangaar. With
  ACCOUNTABILITY  great respect, the City acknowledges the Gabrieleño/Tongva as the First
  (LAND  People of this ancestral and unceded territory of Kuruvungna, a village
  ACKNOWLEDGEMENT)  that we know as Santa Monica. We honor their elders, past and present,
  and the Gabrieleño descendants who are part of the Gabrieleño /Tongva
  tribes.

  We recognize that these peoples are still here, and as settlers and kuyam
  (guests), we recognize our responsibility and obligation to care for their
  land in partnership with them. The City of Santa Monica commits to
  work in partnership with the Gabrieleño/Tongva people to uplift their
  voices and visibility on their ancestral land.

  The City of Santa Monica Statement of Accountability (Land
  Acknowledgement) was read into the record by Councilmember Zwick.

  LEVINE ACT  Pursuant to the Levine Act (Govt Code Section 84308), any party to a
  DISCLOSURE  permit, license, contract, or other entitlement before the Council is
  required to disclose on the record any contribution, including
  aggregated contributions, of more than $500 made by the party or the

  PROJECT  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt the finding that the recommended actions herein do not
  constitute a project subject to the California Environmental Quality
  Act (CEQA) and are exempt under CEQA Guidelines Sections
  15262, and 15306, and file a notice of exemption pursuant to CEQA
  Guideline 15062;
  2. Hold a study session to review and comment on the five Guiding
  Principles for vetting and evaluating the feasibility of features,
  amenities, programs, technical performance requirements, financial
  strategies, phasing, and planning scenarios related to the closure of
  the Airport and alternative land-use scenarios post-closure
  (collectively, “the Santa Monica Airport Conversion Project, or the
  Project”);
  3. Consider the commencement of feasibility analysis for three planning
  scenarios for the Airport Conversion Project (“Phase 3”), based on
  the draft Guiding Principles; and
  4. Provide direction to staff on how to proceed with respect to Phase 3

  Questions asked and answered of staff includedwere: would any of the
  guiding principles preclude exploring housing as an option; was any random
  sampling of residents in Santa Monica done as part of outreach; is staff
  familiar with any research on which populations typically participate in
  community outreach; how can it be determined if the participants of the
  survey are representative of the entire community; how is the project
  engaging with Native people and Native tribes during the input process; how
  will potential conflicts within the guiding principles be reconciled; will there
  be further public engagement in phases 3A and 3B; how is what is being
  presented tonight going to tee up what will be presented to the public in
  phases 3A and 3B; does the city have the discretion to do something else;
  can phased uses be incorporated into the project timeline; are different types
  of financing models being evaluated; is there an example of how a public,
  recreational, cultural facility could be economically self sustaining; can the
  use of a building be changed to be of commercial use that is not currently a
  commercial building; if the city decides to go the route of an environmental
  impact report (EIR) process, will there be a proposed project and a
  reasonable range of economically and legally feasible alternatives, including
  potentially a no project alternative; at what point would the city need to do
  an EIR and what is the timeline and cost; if there are uses in the preferred
  scenario that would require a vote under Measure LC, at what point would it
  need to be put on the ballot; how will the city tease out the differences with
  these three scenarios; as it pertains to housing, how is the preference between
  deed restricted affordable housing versus market rate determined; in terms
  of commercial uses, how is the city teasing out differences between a public
  golf course versus cafes and beer gardens; is the city taking into account legal
  risks from the Surplus Lands Act; is the city consulting with HCD about
  future housing obligations; can small-scale commercial uses be explored
  without requiring a new ballot measure; and will housing be explored among

 Docusign Envelope ID: 54A77BEB-64EA-4BAF-95B5-1184C9BEC1EF

  the non LC compliant uses.

  Considerable discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited to
  concerns about an outdated definition of what environmentalism is based on
  the guiding principles; inserting a clause to state that the project design
  should consider the impact of any future intervention on the natural
  environment and its consequential life cycle, greenhouse gas reduction
  potential, as well as land’s ability to regenerate species and build community
  resilience against climate change; having a day one plan; needing a staged
  process as the city will be unable to implement or fund the final vision for
  what the land will inevitably be used for; exploring the feasibility of the three
  alternative scenarios; encouraging the use of a voting system that ranks
  choices or a preferential voting system instead of a simple plurality; concerns
  about the economic feasibility of the project; needing to meet people of color
  where they are instead of asking them to come to you; reminding the public
  of the realities of when this project will come to fruition; focusing on making
  more sports fields should the city go down the path of building a park; the
  value of mixing recreational space with commercial and housing;
  emphasizing the importance of the financial aspect; being realistic about the
  potential options financially; having a range of alternatives that do not result
  in the permanent sale of airport lands to private parties; needing a long term
  operation strategy when it comes to building a park and who is going to do
  it; the survey not being demographically representative of the Santa Monica
  community; and making sure renters and communities of color are better
  represented in future outreach.

  DIVERSE HOUSING  16.N. Request of Councilmembers Zwick, Zernitskaya, and Hall that,
  CHOICES  in conjunction with necessary updates arising out of SB 450, and in
  order to facilitate diverse housing choices in the City’s highest
  opportunity areas, the City Council directs the City Manager and the
  City Attorney to return with an ordinance to amend the City’s
  regulations governing ministerial approval for certain lot splits and
  duplexes on parcels zoned for single-unit residential by: (1) removing
  the owner-occupancy requirement for lot splits and duplexes and
  clarifying that vacant or demolished parcels, as well as lots with
  approved demolition permits, are eligible for lot splits and duplexes, (2)
  allowing one roof deck per unit, and (3) ensuring that no standard within
  this ordinance or the underlying zoning district shall preclude the
  construction of 2 units, not including ADUs, of at least 1200 square feet
  each. One year after implementation, city staff shall return with a report
  on any impacts of the ordinance, as amended, including data on net new
  housing units permitted, effects on displacement (if any), concentration
  of ownership, and other pertinent information to evaluate its success in
  affirmatively furthering fair housing and creating more affordable
  “missing middle” homes, was approved.
